definitions.interpretation: Evidence labels describe kind, not quality. Most legal/programme facts are guidance; provider offers are reported. No independently evaluated low-income finance effect is asserted.

finance_structures.name: PAYG rent-to-own cooling
finance_structures.mechanism: Equipment access financed over time; device access is linked to payment and ownership follows repayment.
finance_structures.documented_example: Devidayal Solar publishes PAYG refrigeration and lender/EMI/telemetry routes.
finance_structures.activity_status: Published current offer; borrower-level contract/disbursement not audited
finance_structures.instrument: Equipment debt / rent-to-own, subject to lender contract
finance_structures.who_pays: Entrepreneur/household pays lender instalments and operating costs.
finance_structures.who_benefits: Refrigeration users and their customers; this protects products and livelihoods, not necessarily worker heat exposure.
finance_structures.low_income_access_evidence: Company describes rural/first-time-borrower and women-oriented channels; lowest-quintile take-up and sustainable net gains not verified.
conditions_for_fair_use: Disclose total effective price, interest/fees and seasonal cash-flow stress.
Provide a repair/outage and hardship policy; avoid automatic essential-cooling loss.
Use telemetry only for transparent agreed purposes.
finance_structures.risks: Remote locking, spoilage on default, repayment pressure, data use, e-waste and overestimating sales/income.
finance_structures.price_and_terms: Complete comparable installed/lifecycle price, effective borrowing cost and bottom-quintile affordability not established here. Obtain a dated local quote and signed terms; no universal price or FX conversion asserted.
finance_structures.amount_and_currency: No deal, fund-size or tariff amount reproduced in G6; see qualified G3 event records where relevant.
finance_structures.stage: Consumer/product or service delivery mechanism; fund-level comparator explicitly labelled where used.
finance_structures.suits_why: Engineered refrigeration can suit both within equipment ratings; humidity, solar availability, battery/refrigerant service and ambient design matter.
finance_structures.what_to_verify_next: Eligibility, total payments, actual take-up, upkeep, default/exit protection, cash timing and independently assessed access/outcomes.

barriers.name: Rules need inspection, resources and verification
barriers.documented_evidence: Sources distinguish formal requirements from verification, inspection and delivery; roof policy describes occupancy-stage checks and MOM specifies calibrated monitoring.
barriers.market_effect_inference: A published rule may generate limited compliant demand if no authorised inspector, budget, test capacity or remedy is operational.
barriers.suggested_response: Fund inspection and grievance capacity, check certificates against installed/maintained performance and publish safe aggregate implementation data.
barriers.verification_limit: No national enforcement rate or judgement that a named regulator is ineffective is established here.

barriers.name: Product quality, identity and refrigerant provenance
barriers.documented_evidence: UNEP identifies illegal-trade/enforcement and safe-servicing priorities; NEA requires registered regulated goods and supports label verification.
barriers.market_effect_inference: Unverified quality/provenance can undermine promised efficiency, safe servicing, consumer trust and financing.
barriers.suggested_response: Procure verified models and qualified technicians, retain test/chain-of-custody records, warranty remedies and safe end-of-life.
barriers.verification_limit: No country-level counterfeit incidence or allegation against a listed supplier verified; this is a diligence risk, not a prevalence finding.

barriers.name: Installation, competence, parts and maintenance
barriers.documented_evidence: IFC/UNEP identifies supply-chain and installation/maintenance constraints; UNEP’s Malaysia training stresses competence assessment; TechEmerge reports local delivery lessons.
barriers.market_effect_inference: An awarded pilot may not become a dependable service without locally paid capability and spares.
barriers.suggested_response: Finance commissioning, assessed skills, parts inventory, fair paid local jobs and a funded service response.
barriers.verification_limit: Training participation is not verified competence; no region-wide technician shortage count is asserted.

sources.label: ASEAN mARs Guide Version 1 official release

barriers.name: Exposure, loss, performance and beneficiary data gaps
barriers.documented_evidence: Finance synthesis describes information/verification needs; SEWA case records trigger/data mismatch and payment frictions; mARs requires context-based assessment.
barriers.market_effect_inference: Unclear evidence can misprice risk, misidentify beneficiaries or reward proxy measures rather than protection.
barriers.suggested_response: Invest in interoperable public data, relevant calibrated exposure measurement and transparent baselines; minimise sensitive individual records.
barriers.verification_limit: No universal risk algorithm or causal benefit from data alone is established.

barriers.name: Local revenue and currency liability mismatch
barriers.documented_evidence: DFC’s Ecozen summary specifies a local-currency guarantee structure.
barriers.market_effect_inference: For imported equipment or foreign debt, local-currency revenue may not cover depreciating-currency debt or replacement costs; this is a financial inference, not an observed heat-sector default estimate.
barriers.suggested_response: Match currencies where feasible and cost any hedge, pass-through limits and replacement reserves; do not shift opaque FX risk to poor users.
barriers.verification_limit: No comparative cooling-sector FX loss data or universally available local-currency facility verified.

barriers.name: Small contracts and the gap after pilots
barriers.documented_evidence: IFC/UNEP and TechEmerge discuss financing and scale-up challenges facing smaller innovators after early proof.
barriers.market_effect_inference: Small fragmented purchases can be too costly to diligence or too early for asset/venture investors.
barriers.suggested_response: Aggregate compatible demand without excluding local firms, fund preparation and working capital, and secure credible buyer contracts.
barriers.verification_limit: No typical investor minimum ticket or heat-market transaction-cost estimate verified; no assumption all solutions should scale through VC.

barriers.name: Power, water and actual climate suitability
barriers.documented_evidence: Cooling-finance synthesis identifies unreliable power and operating constraints; evaporative-cooling guidance explains dependence on suitable dry-air conditions and water.
barriers.market_effect_inference: Efficient equipment can fail to protect users in outages or unsuitable humidity, or compete for scarce water.
barriers.suggested_response: Use passive load reduction, site-specific moisture/energy design, safe critical-load backup and a sustainable water budget.
barriers.verification_limit: No transferable fan cutoff, evaporative benefit, equipment wattage or water-use figure asserted.

barriers.name: Capital funding and upkeep funding differ
barriers.documented_evidence: SDMF guidelines section 8.5 requires maintenance/upkeep of funded structural or engineering measures to come from other sources; establishment and nonstructural costs also face constraints.
barriers.market_effect_inference: A feasible capital grant may still leave services unfunded after installation.
barriers.suggested_response: Secure a named operating-budget line and accountable caretaker before procurement; match each cost to eligible money.
barriers.verification_limit: This SDMF restriction is not a universal prohibition across every public, donor or climate fund.

sources.label: State Bank Pakistan fan programme circular

barriers.name: Payout, debt and protection mismatches
barriers.documented_evidence: SEWA case describes basis risk and delays; PAYG offer links equipment access to repayment; a guarantee protects the lender’s specified loss position.
barriers.market_effect_inference: Risk can remain with users even when a financial product is described as resilient or inclusive.
barriers.suggested_response: Separate prevention, grants/assistance, retained losses and licensed risk transfer; stress-test default and non-trigger scenarios with users.
barriers.verification_limit: No automatic premium reduction, debt forgiveness, improved health or universal repayment ability inferred.

known: Primary sources document Asian standards, code/plan frameworks, heat-work requirements, public funding constraints and cooling-finance mechanisms.
Singapore enhancements effective December 2026 are future at the research date.
Published Pakistan fan-finance terms identify owner/account requirements and tenant exclusion.
India SDMF guidelines include heatwave mitigation and require separate funding for upkeep.
inferred: Credible demand depends on a duty or need becoming an authorised, funded purchase with accountable delivery.
Finance can reduce upfront barriers but requires separate evidence of affordability, access, risk allocation and protection.
Costed public demand, appropriate subsidies and local maintenance capability may help viable services emerge.
uncertain: Local implementation and enforcement, dedicated municipal HAP appropriations, current eligibility and actual user take-up across most examples.
Bottom-quintile access, total finance burden, default/claims outcomes and independent heat-health impacts.
Transferability across countries and climates; global prevalence of any barrier.
schema_notes: The shared G1–G5 schema has no fields for G6 policies, finance structures, barriers, checks or actor roles. This conditions companion supplies those five arrays explicitly.

heat_economy_g6.json retains the requested six root arrays and segment field shape. Relevant G1 segment descriptors are retained with only G6 sourced demand drivers; market-size arrays are empty and prices are not re-quoted. Other root arrays are unpopulated, not instructions to delete G1–G5 data.
Keep core and conditions/source companions together when importing. G6 is not a new census of businesses, investment events or opportunities.
Countries in a regional assessment framework identify scope, not verified applicant eligibility or identical national law.
method: Read the supplied G6 attachment locally and used G1–G5 as context, preserving the corrected G2 count.
Searched primary public/issuer/operator sources and read relevant originals, recording access failures, future effective dates and historical programme status.
Used OCR for the image-based Telangana policy and visually checked the residential threshold; no advertised cooling, carbon offset or energy-saving figures reused.
Read selected policy/finance, methodology, inclusion and limitation sections of the original IFC/UNEP, MHT, Cambodia and mARs documents; not every page or cited study was appraised.
Separated observed programme/offer rules from inferred demand, conditional transferability and proposed fairness responses.
Did not infer lending access, an open call, a government appropriation, current licence compliance or capital repayability from a broad mission or social benefit.
